title: SlopClient website: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Multiplayer Server List. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Purple + Sora stay in every option.

options.label: Server List
options.lineage: Minecraft's Multiplayer screen: server icons, MOTD lines, ping bars
options.thesis: The website is the Multiplayer screen every player knows by heart, and SlopClient is the server you join.
options.viewport: Centered Multiplayer frame: server entries (Launcher, Client, Microsoft sign-in) with icon, two-line MOTD and ping bars; selected one outlined; Join / Privacy buttons pinned below like the real screen.
options.risk: Can read as a novelty skin if entries only restate copy instead of opening into real sections.

raised.raise: Join runs a live launch log (install, Java, auth, launch) on one shared clock, proving the launcher instead of claiming it.
Selecting an entry isolates it: the rest dim and its section opens, one subject at a time.
Every atom wears the GUI bevel: nav, buttons, toggles, table rows. No stock web component survives.
Sign-in steps are numbered in a strict margin column and deep-linkable.

options.label: Title Screen
options.lineage: Minecraft title screen: rotating panorama, yellow splash text, stacked buttons
options.thesis: The landing page is SlopClient's own custom title screen, the very thing the client mod replaces in-game.
options.viewport: Full-bleed panorama, SlopClient wordmark with a pulsing yellow splash, stacked buttons Features / Sign-in / Privacy.
options.risk: The most familiar move for anything Minecraft; many launcher sites already open on a panorama.

options.label: Live Launch Log
options.lineage: algorave: projected live code driving the room
options.thesis: The page is a running terminal: slopclient commands install and launch a version in real time.
options.viewport: A full-screen log buffer typing 'slopclient launch survival', progress bars filling, the game window popping at the end.
options.case: Holds product clarity (shows the real mechanism) but players identify with the game, not a CLI.
options.risk: Developer-flavoured; hides the client interface players actually want.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: The sign-in chain drawn as particle tracks through detector rings.
options.viewport: One collision, tracks labelled Microsoft / Xbox / XSTS / Minecraft.
options.case: Players and reviewers don't read physics; the metaphor costs clarity.
options.kept: Select one subject to isolate it and dim the rest.

options.label: Lowbrow Panel
options.thesis: Features as lacquered, outlined figures crowding one board.
options.viewport: A crowded airbrushed tableau with a hand-lettered SlopClient panel.
options.case: Loud and hard to scan for reviewers; off-tone for a fair-play launcher.
options.kept: Total outline discipline on every element.
options.risk: Reads as a cheat-client hype page.

options.label: Fold Sequence
options.thesis: One sheet folding step by step into the finished launcher.
options.viewport: A square sheet with numbered fold steps in a margin column.
options.case: Elegant but unrelated to Minecraft players' world.
options.kept: Strict numbered step column with deep-linkable steps.

options.label: Paper Automata
options.thesis: A crank drives a procession of cut-paper features.
options.viewport: A paper stage with the first figure mid-motion.
options.case: Charming, but no identification for players or reviewers.
options.kept: One shared timeline drives every moving part.

options.label: Secession Page
options.thesis: Ornament borders grow in around each section like a clearing.
options.viewport: A symmetrical floral frame around the SlopClient title.
options.case: Conflicts with the dark purple brand; no audience link.
options.kept: Sections arrive by growth along a path, not by fading.
options.risk: Ivory-and-serif territory the brand rules out.

canonCard.label: Launcher site standard
canonCard.thesis: Hero with product screenshot, feature grid, download button and FAQ, like other launcher sites.
canonCard.viewport: Headline left, launcher screenshot right, download button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other launcher site by design.
